title: Fail2ban-compatible auth failure logging
description:
Emit structured log events on authentication failures that fail2ban, AWS WAF, and similar tools can parse to detect and block brute-force attacks.

Why this issue exists:
The NNTP and JMAP services accept credentials over the network. Without structured auth failure events, operators cannot feed failures into fail2ban or WAF rules. A public-facing NNTP port will be probed; operators need tooling to respond.

Scope:
- Emit a structured log event at WARN on every auth failure with fields: event=auth_failure, service=(nntp|jmap|smtp), remote_ip, username (if provided), reason=(bad_password|unknown_user|expired_token|cert_mismatch)
- Emit event=auth_success at DEBUG with the same fields (no password/token content ever logged)
- Emit event=auth_lockout if a configurable per-IP failure threshold is exceeded within a window (default: 10 failures in 60 seconds); this is a log event only, not an enforcement action (enforcement is the network fabric's job)
- Provide a sample fail2ban filter file in docs/ops/ that matches the structured JSON log format
- Log fields must be stable across releases (document them as a stable interface)

Acceptance criteria:
- Five bad passwords from the same IP within 60 seconds produces an auth_lockout log event
- The fail2ban filter in docs/ops/ correctly matches auth_failure events in a real fail2ban test
- No password, token, or credential content appears in any log event
